description: kiln-eml's startup change journal, <game>/kiln/eml/ownership/<stem>.change-journal.json: per package of the committed attempt of a kiln-mode ShroudForge-dialect startup pass, the archive resources its entrypoint wrote, the ones it created and the contents it created, never a value. Separate from the startup outcome (whose strict reader it never touches). Bound to one generation: written only after that generation was published whole, beside the ownership receipt it names, removed before any publication or restore changes the receipt or the live files (kiln-eml's verified BASE and EML's own no-mod restore alike); a startup-cache hit keeps it byte for byte. A reader uses it only when 'generation' is the start's live generation (the startup outcome's archiveSha256). A typed serializer writes the fields in this order. Attribution: a resource is listed for the package whose entrypoint was running when its value was written (any assignment, insertion, removal or clear through its typed values, a copy assigned into it, or its data replaced); code that runs inside an entrypoint is that entrypoint's, whoever wrote it (another package's module function, a finalizer the collector runs then); a write made outside every entrypoint is unattributed; a write into a value detached from its resource still names that resource (a writer may be over-named, never missed). Bounds: at most 4096 entries (changed, created, contents) per package and in 'unattributed', 32768 in all; over that, entries are left out and 'truncated' is true on the package and the journal.

generation.description: kiln-eml's generation digest of the published generation (the startup outcome's and the archive identity's archiveSha256).

receiptSha256.description: SHA-256 of the ownership receipt listing that generation (the outcome's receiptSha256).

dialect.description: The startup dialect whose pass the journal records. The EML dialect writes no journal (its publication removes the previous one).

attempt.description: The committed attempt: only its changes are recorded (a failed first attempt's never).

truncated.description: Some package's or the unattributed bucket's entries were left out (exactly when one of them is truncated).

packages.description: Every package whose entrypoint ran in the committed attempt, in the order they ran (the admitted load order), with nothing listed for one that changed nothing. One entry per id.

unattributed.description: What was written or created while no entrypoint ran; normally empty (the pass runs no Lua between entrypoints).

sfId.description: A ShroudForge identifier, as sfi-state.schema.json's sfId.

guid.description: A GUID as the game's archive and ShroudForge's Resource.guid write it (lower-case).

version.description: The plan's version of the package (null when empty).

kind.description: The plan's kind: a ShroudForge package or an EML package that ShroudForge's pass runs.

contentSha256.description: The package folder's content digest the launch plan froze (with id and version: the package identity effect replay keys on).

settingsSha256.description: Its settings document's digest the launch plan froze.

typeHash.description: The resource's type hash (the qualified type name's FNV-1a), 8 lower-case hex digits.

createdBy.description: For a resource another package created in this pass: that package and its ordinal (the created resource's name across runs); null for an archive resource.

changedList.description: The resources the entrypoint wrote, in resource-key order (GUID bytes, type hash, part), each once; never one the package created itself.

typeHash.description: The resource's type hash (the qualified type name's FNV-1a), 8 lower-case hex digits.

explicit.description: The package gave the GUID and part (stable across runs); false: drawn at random (differs per publication; the ordinal names it).

createdList.description: The resources the entrypoint created, in creation order, ordinals 1, 2, ... (the ones over the bound are the last, left out). A created resource is named <package id>:<ordinal> across runs, which holds while the package creates in the same order: the Lua runtime seeds its string hashing anew for every run, so creations made while walking a table with string keys (pairs, next) can be numbered differently from run to run. A consumer matches a created resource by (package id, version, contentSha256, typeHash, part, ordinal) and expects such a mismatch; an explicit GUID is always stable.

guid.description: The content's hash as a GUID (Content.guid): content-derived, the same for the same bytes.

size.description: Its size in bytes (also the GUID's first group, little-endian).

contentList.description: The contents the entrypoint created (create_content), each once, in the order first created.
